github_issue.notes: Every factual claim verified against v1.0.21: the checkbox starts checked (IAMGroups.tsx:341), management_create_group defaults create_in_idp=True (management_routes.py:422), and both legacy Form() defaults are True (server_routes.py:2248,3464), so the problem statement and motivation are repo-grounded, not generic. Acceptance criteria are genuinely testable (initial unchecked state, reset path, preview contains create_in_idp:false, no IdP call, explicit-true back-compat) and the response-id-equals-name oracle in the local-only branch matches the handler. Largest gap: the parallel silent-IdP-write default at /api/servers/groups/import (server_routes.py:3800, body.get('create_in_idp', ...True)) is the same footgun and is never mentioned, and there is no note about communicating the API default change to existing consumers. Risk awareness is solid on the two real failure modes (silent IdP mutation, hard failure under restricted IdP scopes) with explicit, justified non-goals.

lld.notes: This is a decision-ready design: every step names the exact file, line, and replacement (useState at :341, resetForm at :378-382, EXAMPLE_SCOPE_JSON at :88, management_routes.py:421-424, server_routes.py:2248/3464 plus docstring and curl text at 3479/3490), and I verified each cited location exists with the described content, including the untyped GroupCreateRequest.scope_config (schemas/management.py:115) that makes a schema change unnecessary. The plan correctly identifies the stale test test_create_group_default_creates_in_idp at test_management_routes.py:698 and pins the exact replacement import_group kwargs, which I confirmed match the handler (description='' via 'or ""', group_mappings=[name]). Two accuracy nits: the CLI is cited as 'registry/cli' when the real callers are api/registry_client.py:1937 and api/registry_management.py:861 (the substance, that the CLI always sends the field explicitly and already defaults --idp to false, is correct), and the test draft mocks GETs to /api/virtual-servers and /api/agents that IAMGroups never fires. Risk handling covers the reset-path footgun, no-migration argument, existing audit logging, and a rejected config-knob alternative, but never analyzes legacy callers that omit create_in_idp nor the import endpoint's own True default.

review.notes: This is a real review, not role-play: all three must-fix findings are genuine and verified in the repo (resetForm setCreateInIdp(true) at IAMGroups.tsx:381 including the after-create call at :407; the old-default-pinning test at test_management_routes.py:698; EXAMPLE_SCOPE_JSON true at :88), each with consequence, concrete fix, and tracked resolution in the revised LLD. Cited details hold up, including TestManagementDeleteGroupLocalOnly (line 735), the docstring/curl drift at server_routes.py:3479/3490, and the audit log lines at 425-428/456. Weakness: every persona approves the core scope without probing the one open compat question, who calls /api/internal/create-group or /api/servers/groups/create while omitting create_in_idp (asserted unaffected rather than investigated), and the grep would have surfaced the untouched default-True at server_routes.py:3800. Recommendations are prioritized and actionable, with deferrals (a11y wiring, docs) explicitly justified.

testing.notes: The plan pins the exact behaviors the issue promised at the right levels: Jest assertions on the initial unchecked state and the post-reset state, a backend default test asserting mock_iam.create_group.assert_not_called() plus exact import_group kwargs (mechanically valid given the get_iam_manager patching fixture), curl positive/negative flows, a backwards-compat matrix, and an E2E restricted-credentials journey that maps to the issue's second failure mode. Commands agree with the repo (uv run pytest on tests/unit/api/test_management_routes.py, npm test with react-scripts, docker-compose.yml exists at root), and the response oracle id==group-name matches the handler's local-only branch. Oracles are concrete throughout (expected statuses, no IdP group, checkbox states), though several UX checks depend on manual IdP-console inspection and the Jest mocks fire at /api/virtual-servers and /api/agents endpoints the component never calls. Rollback reasoning (local-only groups remain deletable, no migration to undo) is correct and proportionate.

implementation.notes: The patch implements the full design end to end: all six LLD steps land (frontend state/reset/example JSON, management default, both legacy Form() defaults plus docstring and curl text, rewritten backend test, new Jest file with a bonus reset-reopen case), every hunk's context matches the real source byte-for-byte, and the rewritten test's expected import_group kwargs are exactly what the handler produces. The material defect is packaging: as submitted, plain git apply fails with 'corrupt patch' because the IAMGroups.tsx third hunk header declares 7 old lines but supplies 6 (missing a trailing blank context line), and the test-file hunk header (23/17) also disagrees with its body (~31/35); I confirmed the content is right by running git apply --recount --check, which passes, but this contradicts implementation.md's claim that 'git apply --check passed'. The summary is otherwise truthful and precise, including per-file counts I re-derived exactly (+113/-20 across 5 files), honest non-execution disclosure, and justified exclusions (docs, a11y, release note).

verdict: An unusually well-grounded, repo-accurate submission whose design, review, and tests all verify against v1.0.21 and whose patch is semantically complete and correct, with the largest material limitation being that the submitted diff fails plain git apply due to miscounted hunk headers (recoverable only via --recount), which also falsifies the summary's verification claim.
